key_insight: This paper introduces Panda, an unsupervised framework for detecting pelvic anomalies in real-time MRI without needing rare, hand-labeled adverse-event examples. It aims to make anomaly detection practical in settings where supervised methods are not feasible.
problem_solved: It addresses the challenge of spotting abnormal pelvic events during MRI despite motion, tissue deformation, and instrument artifacts, especially when anomalies are rare, diverse, and hard to annotate.
method: Uses a Dinomaly-based unsupervised anomaly detection framework.
Learns the normal appearance of pelvic MR images and flags deviations as potential anomalies.
Designed for real-time use in dynamic MRI environments where supervised labels are unavailable or unreliable.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, this shows how unsupervised detection can be applied to high-stakes medical imaging problems with scarce labels. It may enable earlier warning systems for image-guided procedures and improve safety in pelvic MRI workflows.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram showing normal-image training and anomaly scoring at inference
Before/after MR image examples highlighting detected anomalies
Icon set for motion, deformation, and instrument artifacts
Simple comparison chart: supervised vs unsupervised anomaly detection
paper_title: Panda: Unsupervised Pelvic Anomaly Detection for Real-Time MR Imaging
paper_authors: Anika Knupfer, Maximilian Lindholz, Johanna Paula Müller, Jordina Aviles Verdera, Smiti Tripathy
